items.criterion: The recap's total runtime is between 158 and 175 seconds inclusive.
items.why: Golden human reference recap runs 166.32s; v1 prompt requires recap runtime within ±5% of golden. 158-175s also sits inside the curator's short_140_180s runtime band.
items.check: Read the duration from the submitted recap file (e.g., via ffprobe-equivalent). Pass if 158.0 ≤ duration_seconds ≤ 175.0.

items.criterion: The submitted recap is a playable mp4 video file with at least one video stream and at least one audio stream.
items.why: Deliverable contract; an audio-less file would let the agent escape the source-audio policy.
items.check: Probe streams of the submitted recap file. Pass if codec is h264 (or compatible mp4 video codec) AND at least one audio stream is present.

items.criterion: The recap's display aspect ratio is 9:16 vertical at target resolution 1080×1920 with no letterbox bars and no pillarbox bars added by the editor.
items.why: Brief commissions a 1080×1920 vertical (9:16) deliverable for TikTok / Reels; this item must agree with V-NOT-VERTICAL. The source is 16:9 broadcast that must be reframed up to vertical.
items.check: Inspect the first and middle frames of the recap. Pass if ffprobe width=1080 AND height=1920 (or, equivalently, aspect ratio width/height in [0.5, 0.6]) AND no added black bars cover more than 5% of frame height or width. Judge cites the recap timestamp(s) of the frame(s) inspected.

items.criterion: A figure-skating jump that is a combination of two jumps in sequence (the skater takes off, lands, and immediately takes off again into a second jump without putting the free foot down between them) appears within the first 35 seconds of the recap.
items.why: Source calibration: the triple-Lutz / triple-toe-loop combination occurs at ~01:17 in source and is the routine's signature opening element. Recap should establish the routine with this combination near the start.
items.check: Watch the first 35 seconds of the recap and identify whether any single visible jumping pass clearly shows two rotational jumps performed back-to-back without an intervening glide. Judge cites the recap timestamp where this combination appears.

items.criterion: At least one shot in the recap that contains skating-routine footage (skater on the ice performing the program) is held continuously for at least 5 seconds without a cut.
items.why: A 5-second uncut hold is the simplest measurable test for "showed the routine as one performance rather than a montage". Anything below 5s lets quick-cut jump compilations sneak through. This item subsumes the earlier V-CONTINUITY-MARKER (which rewarded a 3-second non-jump hold); the 5-second uncut routine-shot test is strictly stricter and the two were semantically overlapping. Weight folded from the dropped V-CONTINUITY-MARKER.
items.check: Watch the recap. Find the longest uncut shot of on-ice routine material. Pass if its duration is ≥5.0 seconds. Judge cites the recap start-and-end timestamps of that longest shot.

items.criterion: The recap's on-ice routine footage shows the skater wearing a predominantly royal-blue or cobalt-blue dress; she is not predominantly wearing any other costume color.
items.why: Source calibration: Yuna's free-skate costume is royal blue with silver crystals. If the recap shows her in black, white, or any other dress during on-ice routine footage, it has imported footage from outside the source (e.g., short program, exhibition, or different competition), which the source does not contain.
items.check: Sample the on-ice routine frames of the recap. Pass if the skater's dress is predominantly blue in ≥80% of routine-footage frames sampled. Judge cites recap timestamps of two frames where the dress is clearly visible.

items.criterion: The recap contains a shot of the skater holding her final pose at the end of the program, typically with hands at chest or clasped, standing still, music having ended, audience applauding.
items.why: Source calibration: final pose at ~05:03 in source. The pose-to-applause moment is the climactic end of the on-ice section before the score reveal; outcome highlights should include it.
items.check: Watch the recap. Identify a still-standing pose held by the skater that is clearly the END of her routine (not a mid-routine choreographic pose). Judge cites the recap timestamp where this pose appears.

items.criterion: The recap does not show any other competitor skating a routine; any non-Yuna skater shown (if any) appears only in cutaways such as crowd, coaches, or medal-context, not performing on the ice.
items.why: Source contains only Yuna's skate. Importing another skater's footage would be hallucinated content not available in the source.
items.check: Watch the recap. Pass if no on-ice routine footage of any skater other than Yuna Kim (the woman in the royal-blue dress in this recap) appears. Judge cites recap timestamps of any non-Yuna skater shown, or notes "none seen" if absent.

items.criterion: The recap does not show a medal-ceremony, podium, or victory-ceremony scene (e.g., a podium with three athletes on tiered steps, an athlete being handed a medal, a medal lifted to the camera, a flag-raising).
items.why: Source does not contain any medal ceremony or podium footage. Including such material would mean the agent has fabricated or imported content outside the provided source.
items.check: Watch the entire recap. Pass if there is no shot of a podium, no shot of any athlete with a gold/silver/bronze medal physically present or being awarded, and no flag-raising. Judge cites the recap timestamp of any such shot, or notes "none seen".

items.criterion: A scoreboard, results graphic, or overlay containing the numerical total score "228.56" (or the broken-out free-skate score "150.06") is visible on screen for at least 1 continuous second in the recap.
items.why: Source calibration: scoreboard graphic with FS 150.06 / Total 228.56 appears at ~07:35 in source and is the recap's intended climax. This is the central narrative beat for an outcome highlight.
items.check: Watch the recap. Identify any moment where the digits "228.56" OR "150.06" are clearly legible on screen (as part of a scoreboard, lower-third, or overlay graphic) for ≥1 second. Judge cites the recap timestamp where this graphic appears and the duration it is on screen.

items.criterion: An audible spoken announcement of the score in the recognizable register of a live arena PA announcer (formal Olympic-rink delivery with arena reverb) is present in the recap's audio track, containing the words "228.56", "150.06", "season's best", or "currently in first place".
items.why: Source calibration: PA announcer at ~07:35 says "She has earned 150.06 points in the free program, which is a new season's best. Yu-Na Kim has a total score of 228.56 points and is currently in first place." This is the audio climax that pairs with the scoreboard. The diversity constraint (source_audio_only) forbids any added third-party narrator voice; an added narrator reading the score does NOT satisfy this item, the spoken phrase must come from the source PA broadcast (judged by arena-reverb signature and live-rink delivery).
items.check: Listen to the recap's audio. Pass if at least one clearly audible spoken sentence containing "228.56", "150.06", "season's best", or "currently in first place" is present AND the voice is recognizable as a live arena PA announcer (audible arena reverb, public-address compression, in-venue ambience). A clean studio-recorded narrator voice with no arena reverb does NOT pass. Judge cites the recap timestamp of the spoken phrase and notes audible acoustic characteristics (reverb, ambience).

items.criterion: The kiss-and-cry beat is visible in the recap: the skater is shown seated (not skating) in a small area with team-colored jackets visible, accompanied by another person (her coach), reacting to a scoreboard.
items.why: Source calibration: kiss-and-cry runs ~07:13-08:06 in source, with Yuna in a white Team-Korea jacket beside Brian Orser in a red jacket. This beat is what visually anchors the score reveal in a highlight package.
items.check: Watch the recap. Pass if at least one shot clearly shows the skater seated (not on the ice, not standing) in a small enclosed area with another person beside her, in what is recognizable as a post-skate waiting area. Judge cites the recap timestamp where this shot appears.

items.criterion: The very last frame of the recap (the final frame before fade-out / end-card / file end) shows either a scoreboard with numerical scores visible OR a kiss-and-cry shot of the skater seated beside her coach.
items.why: Brief requires the score reveal to be the closing beat. Outcome-highlight convention is that the recap *destination* is the score, not a triumphant skating moment. Ending on a jump landing or final-pose hold misframes the story as "she skated well" rather than "she won gold with a record score".
items.check: Inspect the very last frame of the recap before fade-out or end-card. Pass if that frame contains either (a) any scoreboard or results graphic with at least one numerical score visible, or (b) a shot of the skater seated (not on ice) in a small enclosed area with another person beside her (the kiss-and-cry). Judge cites the recap timestamp of the last frame and describes its visible content.

items.criterion: If the recap places any on-screen text label identifying a specific named jump element ("lutz", "flip", "salchow", "axel", "toe loop", "loop", "combination", "triple", "double") on a jumping pass, the label placed on the recap's first labeled jumping pass is consistent with a triple-Lutz / triple-toe-loop combination (e.g., "3Lz+3T", "triple Lutz - triple toe", "opening combo: 3Lz+3T", "triple Lutz/triple toe loop combination"). If no on-screen jump labels appear anywhere in the recap, this item passes by default.
items.why: Source calibration: the routine's first jumping pass at ~01:17 is the 3Lz+3T combination. This item rewards correct labeling without forcing the agent to label at all; the corresponding penalty item N-WRONG-JUMP-LABEL handles mislabeling. Note: only on-screen text labels are considered (added narrator VO is forbidden by S-ADDED-VO-PRESENT; the source PA never names jumps in this file).
items.check: Watch the recap. Identify the first jumping pass that carries any on-screen text label naming a jump. Pass if that label is consistent with "triple Lutz - triple toe loop combination" (synonyms: 3Lz+3T, 3Lz/3T, triple Lutz triple toe). Also pass if NO on-screen jump text labels appear anywhere in the recap. Judge cites the recap timestamp of the first labeled jump (or notes "no labeled jumps").

items.criterion: The recap does not display any scoreboard graphic, results table, or score overlay showing a numerical total score that is not 228.56 or 150.06.
items.why: Source calibration: the only score event in source is FS 150.06 / Total 228.56 at ~07:35. Any other total (e.g., 230, 225, 228.5, or the 78.50 short-program total) is either fabricated or imported from outside-source footage the agent does not have.
items.check: Watch the recap. Identify every scoreboard, results table, or score overlay shown. Pass if every numerical total displayed (as a "TOTAL", "SCORE", "OVERALL", or similar header) is either 228.56 or 150.06. Other component values that appear within a single scoreboard (TES 78.30, PCS 71.76, Deductions 0.00) are acceptable as part of the legitimate scoreboard. Judge cites recap timestamps and the numeric values shown on any score graphic.

items.criterion: The recap contains no on-screen text overlay that asserts a false identity claim about the recap's subject: any name other than Yuna Kim / Kim Yu-Na / Yu-Na Kim / 김연아, any country other than the Republic of Korea / South Korea / KOR / 대한민국, or any Games / venue / year other than Vancouver 2010 / 2010 Vancouver Olympic Winter Games / Pacific Coliseum.
items.why: Outcome highlights routinely add overlay text with name, country, and venue. A single wrong identity overlay (wrong name, wrong country, or wrong Games) is a hallucination failure on a recap of one of the most-watched single performances in Olympic figure-skating history. Note: added narrator VO is forbidden by S-ADDED-VO-PRESENT; only on-screen text overlays and the source PA are in scope here, and the source PA correctly identifies Yuna by name and country.
items.check: Watch the recap. Read every on-screen text overlay (titles, lower-thirds, end cards, captions). Pass if no single text overlay contains a name, country, or Games identifier that contradicts {skater = Yuna Kim / Kim Yu-Na / Yu-Na Kim / 김연아; country = Republic of Korea / South Korea / KOR / Korea / 대한민국; Games = Vancouver 2010 / 2010 Vancouver Olympic Winter Games / Pacific Coliseum}. Standard romanizations and Korean script are acceptable. If no name/country/Games identifier appears in any overlay, this item passes by default. Judge cites the recap timestamp and content of the first false identity claim found, or notes "no identity claims".

items.criterion: At least one spoken-word fragment of the source PA announcer (English-language, formal Olympic-rink register with audible arena reverb) is audible somewhere in the recap and is not drowned out by music or sound effects.
items.why: Source PA audio appears at the top ("...representing the Republic of Korea, Yu-Na Kim") and at the score reveal ("...currently in first place"). Preserving at least one such announcement is the audio identity of the source.
items.check: Listen to the entire recap. Pass if at least one spoken-word PA-announcement fragment (recognizable by formal rink-register and arena reverb) is audible. The same PA-call fragment used to pass N-PA-SCORE-CALL satisfies this item. Judge cites the recap timestamp where the PA voice is audible.

items.criterion: During on-ice routine footage in the recap, music is audible on the audio track (the music can be the source Gershwin "Concerto in F" or any music; this item only checks that the routine is not played in silence).
items.why: A skating routine played silent is unwatchable; the routine's tempo is the music. The brief explicitly requires music during the routine.
items.check: Listen to the recap during any on-ice routine segment (skater performing on ice). Pass if music is audibly present (any instrumental or scored music, not crowd-only) during routine footage. Judge cites a recap timestamp where routine footage is on screen AND music is heard.

items.criterion: Across the body of the recap (excluding any opening title-card lead-in and any end-card tail), the diegetic source audio mix, instrumental music, arena crowd ambience, and PA announcer fragments, is audibly continuous: there is no extended (>2-second) span of total silence inside the body, and there is no audible swap to a different audio program (different music genre, studio narration bed) replacing the source mix. (Weight raised from +2 to +5 in QC Pass B to absorb the downgraded S-ADDED-VO-PRESENT penalty, diversity-constraint audio_policy is a craft requirement, not a comprehension-breaker.)
items.why: Diversity constraint: audio_policy=source_audio_only. The recap must preserve the broadcast's diegetic mix as a continuous bed, not stitch silent edits or duck under a new narration bed. This is the positive complement to the S-ADDED-VO-PRESENT penalty.
items.check: Listen to the recap from start to end. Identify every span of total silence (no music, no PA, no crowd) and every span where the audible audio program clearly switches identity. Pass if NO single silence span exceeds 2.0 seconds inside the body AND the audible audio program remains consistent (same orchestral music idiom, same arena ambience signature) across the body. Judge cites the recap timestamps of the longest silence and of any audio-program switch, or notes "audio is continuous source-mix throughout".

items.criterion: During on-ice routine footage in the recap, the audible music is consistent with orchestral, classical, or piano-driven Gershwin-style material (NOT modern pop, hip-hop, EDM, cinematic-trailer score, ambient drone, or stock highlight-reel beats).
items.why: Source music is Gershwin's "Concerto in F" (orchestral, jazz-inflected, with piano lead). The brief forbids swapping the music bed for a generic highlight-reel track.
items.check: Listen to the recap during any on-ice routine segment. Pass if the audible music is orchestral / classical / piano-led (recognizably acoustic instrumental in a 1920s-American-classical idiom); FAIL if the music is electronic, hip-hop, modern pop, contemporary cinematic trailer score, EDM, or stock highlight-reel beats. Judge cites the recap timestamp and identifies the musical idiom.

items.criterion: At the recap moment where the score announcement is spoken (containing "228.56", "150.06", "season's best", or "currently in first place"), the announcer's words are intelligible to a listener and are not obscured by simultaneous voice-over, music swell, or muting.
items.why: The score-announce moment is the audio climax. Talking over it, muting it, or burying it under a music swell is the single most common amateur edit and is what separates an outcome highlight from a generic montage.
items.check: Identify the recap timestamp(s) where the score-announce phrase is spoken (the same content checked by N-PA-SCORE-CALL). Listen at that timestamp. Pass if the spoken phrase is clearly intelligible to a listener (the listener can hear and understand "228.56" or "currently in first place" or the equivalent words) AND no simultaneous human voice-over, simultaneous music swell, or audio muting renders it unintelligible. If N-PA-SCORE-CALL fails (no source-PA score announcement is present in the recap audio at all), this item FAILS by default. Judge cites the recap timestamp of the score-announce moment and describes the audio state.

items.criterion: No persistent overlay element, a scoreboard widget, a lower-third name strap, a chapter / section title card, or any other graphic that is NOT part of the source broadcast's own scoreboard graphic at the score reveal, remains continuously visible on screen across more than 80% of the recap's total runtime.
items.why: Diversity constraint: output_shape=single_concat. The brief calls for one continuous cut of the program with no chapter cards, no scoreboard widget riding the whole runtime. (Downgraded from V-UNEXPECTED-OVERLAY-PERSISTS [-20] in QC Pass B, single_concat is a craft preference, not a comprehension-breaker.)
items.check: Inspect frames sampled approximately every 10 seconds across the entire recap. Count how many sampled frames contain a persistent graphic overlay element (a fixed-position scoreboard widget, a fixed-position lower-third name strap, or a chapter / section title card) that is NOT the broadcast's own at-source scoreboard graphic during the score-reveal beat. Pass if such overlay is present in fewer than 80% of sampled frames. Judge cites the recap timestamps sampled and the overlay element observed (or notes "no persistent overlay").

items.criterion: The recap presents Yuna's free skate as a rapid-jump-cut montage: more than 12 shot transitions occur within any single rolling 30-second window of routine footage, OR no single uncut shot of routine footage in the recap reaches 4 seconds in duration.
items.why: This is the dominant failure mode for sports outcome highlights: collapsing a 4-minute routine into a fast-cut jumps montage. The brief explicitly forbids this. If the recap presents jumps as quick cuts without showing the routine as one continuous performance, deduct -50; this is the single largest penalty because it breaks the entire outcome-highlight premise. The threshold of 12 transitions / 30s is roughly one cut every 2.5 seconds, which is the boundary between "montage" and "highlight cut" in broadcast convention.
items.check: Walk through the recap and count shot transitions (any cut, dissolve, or fade that ends one shot and begins another) within the segments containing on-ice routine footage. Trigger this penalty if EITHER (a) any rolling 30-second window of routine footage contains >12 transitions, OR (b) the longest uncut shot of routine footage is <4.0 seconds. Judge cites the recap timestamp range of the 30s window with peak transition density (or the longest routine shot duration if (b) triggers).

items.criterion: The recap contains no visible scoreboard showing "228.56" or "150.06" AND no audible spoken announcement containing "228.56", "150.06", "season's best", or "currently in first place".
items.why: An outcome highlight that omits the outcome is not an outcome highlight. The score reveal is the central narrative beat; the brief explicitly requires it as the closing moment. If the kiss-and-cry / 228.56 scoreboard moment is absent in BOTH video and audio, deduct -30.
items.check: Trigger this penalty if BOTH (a) N-SCOREBOARD-228 fails (no "228.56" or "150.06" graphic visible for ≥1 second anywhere in the recap), AND (b) N-PA-SCORE-CALL fails (no PA-register spoken phrase containing "228.56", "150.06", "season's best", or "currently in first place" anywhere in the recap). Judge reports whether each of (a) and (b) failed and cites recap timestamps of any partial score-reveal material if present.

items.criterion: The recap's aspect ratio is not 9:16 vertical, it is 16:9 horizontal or any aspect ratio wider than tall. A vertical recap is the structural deliverable for TikTok / Reels distribution; a horizontal recap fails the platform brief entirely.
items.why: Brief commissions a 1080×1920 vertical (9:16) deliverable for TikTok / Instagram Reels. A horizontal cut, even if perfectly edited otherwise, cannot ship to the commissioned platform.
items.check: Judge probes the recap's frame width and height. Pass (deduction fires) if and only if the frame height is not strictly greater than the frame width.

items.criterion: The recap is a true vertical reframe but the crop is wrong-centered: across the routine-action frames (frames where Yuna is skating, jumping, spinning, in a layback / spiral / Biellmann position, or at the kiss-and-cry score reveal), her full body silhouette does not stay inside the visible vertical frame AND/OR the 228.56 score reveal is not fully visible in the kiss-and-cry beat.
items.why: A 9:16 reframe from a 16:9 broadcast figure-skating source forces the editor to track the skater up the height of the rink; a wrong-centered crop loses the arms at a layback's full extension, clips the landing leg after a triple, or hides the score reveal at the kiss-and-cry. Either failure breaks the routine's vertical readability or its scored payoff. This item assumes a true vertical reframe; letterbox-cheat output (horizontal content padded into a 9:16 canvas) is covered separately by V-LETTERBOX-CHEAT.
items.check: Judge samples the recap at 1 fps across all routine-action frames (frames where Yuna is skating, jumping, spinning, in a layback / spiral / Biellmann position, or at the kiss-and-cry score reveal). For each sampled frame, judge confirms whether Yuna's full body silhouette stays inside the visible vertical frame AND, for kiss-and-cry frames, whether the 228.56 score reveal is fully visible. Pass (deduction fires) if and only if MORE than 20% of sampled routine-action frames clip Yuna's arms / leg extension / jump apex / landing leg OR the kiss-and-cry score reveal of 228.56 is cropped outside the frame.

items.criterion: The recap's frame dimensions are vertical (height > width) but the actual cinematic figure-skating video content sits in a horizontal band occupying only the middle of the vertical frame, with padding bars (black, scoreboard graphics, branding cards, caption strips, blurred background, OR any combination) above and below the active video content. This is a "Reels template" letterbox cheat: technically-vertical-but-actually-horizontal content padded into a 9:16 canvas.
items.why: Brief commissions a TRUE vertical reframe of the 16:9 broadcast figure-skating source. A horizontal clip with vertical padding still ships the wrong viewing experience: viewers see a small horizontal skating strip surrounded by graphics, not a vertical reframe of Yuna's routine. The author has not actually done the reframe work; they have padded the source into a vertical container. (QC Pass B: weight reduced from -50 to -15, the viewer still sees the action.)
items.check: Judge samples the recap at 5 timestamps (~10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%) and identifies the bounding box of the active cinematic skating content (excluding scoreboard widgets, branding cards, caption strips, black bars, blurred backgrounds). Pass (deduction fires) if and only if the active video content's vertical extent occupies less than 75% of the frame height in 3 or more of the 5 samples, i.e., the vertical padding (top + bottom non-video region) consistently exceeds 25% of total frame height.
